name: Pylyp Orlyk's Campaign in Right-Bank Ukraine (1711) (C0027)

techniques.comment: The collapse of the anti-Moscow coalition from within: on the Right Bank, the Tatar allies betrayed the Cossacks and turned to seizing the civilian population – "the Tatars, disobeying Orlyk, scattered in raiding parties and began taking yasyr captives across Ukrainian villages"(Citation: Мазепинці 1885). Orlyk himself wrote to the Swedish king: "What atrocities unheard of under the moon did the wild Tatars then commit!"(Citation: Мазепинці 1885).

The empire's forcible retention of the Right Bank: the Bila Tserkva fortress with its Muscovite garrison held out, and the campaign collapsed after the Tatars' betrayal – "Orlyk retreated without taking Bila Tserkva"(Citation: Мазепинці 1885), and his army disintegrated.
